raw_segments.text: The first direct attempts of the proletariat to attain its own ends made in times of universal excitement when feudal society was being overthrown.
These attempts necessarily failed, owing to the then undeveloped state of the proletariat,
as well as to the absence of the economic conditions for its emancipation, conditions that had yet to be produced,
and could be produced by the impending bourgeois epoch alone.
The revolutionary literature that accompanied these first movements of the proletariat had necessarily a reactionary character.
It inculcated universal asceticism and social leveling in its crudest form.
